1.topic: Àkọsílẹ̀ ìpín púpọ̀ lórí kókó kan (Writing a composition in paragraphs)
1.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. plan and write a composition of three paragraphs (introduction, body, conclusion) on a given topic;
2. start each paragraph with a clear topic sentence and support it with details;
3. use linking words (ní àkọ́kọ́, bákan náà, yàtọ̀ sí èyí, nítorí náà) to join ideas.

## Materials

A model essay on a chart, strips with the linking words, a planning grid on the board (Topic sentence, Detail 1, Detail 2), notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Display two short texts on the same topic: one a single block of sentences and one in three clear paragraphs. Ask which is easier to read in Yoruba and why. Link the answer to paragraphs.

## Development

1. Revise from JSS2: ìbẹ̀rẹ̀, àárín and ìparí. Explain that in JSS3 each part is a paragraph with a purpose: the introduction states the topic, the body gives reasons or examples, and the conclusion sums up.
2. Show the model essay "Ìmọ́tótó" and mark the topic sentence of each paragraph. Show how the details prove the topic sentence.
3. Teach the linking words: ní àkọ́kọ́ (first of all), bákan náà (likewise), yàtọ̀ sí èyí (apart from this), nítorí náà (therefore).
4. Use the planning grid for a new topic, "Pàtàkì ìkàwé" (the importance of reading). Pupils suggest the topic sentence, two details and a conclusion.
5. Pupils write their draft in twenty minutes. Walk around and prompt: Is the topic clear in the first sentence? Are the sentences complete? Are the marks correct?
6. Read two drafts aloud. The class says what makes each paragraph clear.

## Class activity

Paragraph builders. Give each group the jumbled sentences of an essay. They arrange them into introduction, body and conclusion, and underline the linking words.

## Evaluation

1. What does a topic sentence do?
2. Name two linking words and say what each does.
3. How do you know that a conclusion is a good one?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Pàtàkì ìmọ́tótó: àpẹẹrẹ àkọsílẹ̀ ìpín mẹ́ta
reading.content:
# Àkọsílẹ̀ ìpín púpọ̀

Àkọsílẹ̀ tí ó dára ní àkọlé àti ìpín mẹ́ta. Ìpín kọ̀ọ̀kan ní iṣẹ́ tirẹ̀.

## Ìpín mẹ́ta

1. **Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ (introduction):** ó sọ kókó àkọsílẹ̀ náà ní kedere.
2. **Àárín (body):** ó fúnni ní ìdí tàbí àpẹẹrẹ tí ó ń tì èrò náà lẹ́yìn.
3. **Ìparí (conclusion):** ó ṣe àkópọ̀ ohun tí a sọ, ó sì fún olùkàwé ní ìmọ̀ràn tàbí èrò ìkẹyìn.

Gbólóhùn àkọ́kọ́ nínú ìpín kọ̀ọ̀kan ni **gbólóhùn kókó (topic sentence)**. Ó sọ èrò pàtàkì ìpín náà.

## Àpẹẹrẹ

**Pàtàkì ìmọ́tótó**

Ìmọ́tótó ṣe pàtàkì fún ìlera wa. Ó jẹ́ ohun tí gbogbo ènìyàn gbọdọ̀ ṣe lójoojúmọ́, ní ilé àti ní ilé ìwé.

Ní àkọ́kọ́, bí a bá ń fọ ọwọ́ wa kí a tó jẹun, a kò ní ní àìsàn inú. Bákan náà, bí a bá ń gbá ilé wa lójoojúmọ́, kòkòrò kò ní pọ̀ nínú rẹ̀. Yàtọ̀ sí èyí, àyíká tí ó mọ́ máa ń dùn wò, ó sì ń mú inú wa dùn.

Nítorí náà, ó yẹ kí gbogbo wa máa tọ́jú ìmọ́tótó. Bí a bá ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, ìlera wa yóò dára, àyíká wa yóò sì lẹ́wà.

### Ṣíṣàyẹ̀wò àpẹẹrẹ

- **Ìpín kìíní** bẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú gbólóhùn kókó: "Ìmọ́tótó ṣe pàtàkì fún ìlera wa."
- **Ìpín kejì** ní àlàyé mẹ́ta tí a so pọ̀ pẹ̀lú ní àkọ́kọ́, bákan náà àti yàtọ̀ sí èyí.
- **Ìpín kẹta** bẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú nítorí náà, ó sì parí àkọsílẹ̀.

## Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| ní àkọ́kọ́ | bẹ̀rẹ̀ àlàyé àkọ́kọ́ |
| bákan náà | fi àlàyé kún un (likewise) |
| yàtọ̀ sí èyí | fi nǹkan mìíràn kún un (apart from this) |
| nítorí náà | fi ìparí hàn (therefore) |

## Bí a ṣe ń ṣètò àkọsílẹ̀

1. Yan àkọlé tí ó ṣe kedere.
2. Kọ gbólóhùn kókó fún ìpín kọ̀ọ̀kan.
3. Kọ àlàyé méjì tàbí mẹ́ta fún ìpín àárín.
4. Kọ ìparí tí ó so ohun gbogbo pọ̀.
5. Ka a padà. Ṣàtúnṣe àmì ohùn, ẹ̀ṣẹ̀-ìsàlẹ̀ àti ìlànà gbólóhùn.

## Àwọn àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

- Fífi èrò púpọ̀ tí kò jọra sínú ìpín kan.
- Àìlo ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀.
- Ìparí tí ó bẹ̀rẹ̀ èrò tuntun.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Ìpín kọ̀ọ̀kan ní èrò kan ṣoṣo. Gbólóhùn kókó ń sọ èrò náà, àwọn àlàyé sì ń tì í lẹ́yìn.

2.topic: Ọ̀rọ̀ ẹbí, iṣẹ́ àti ẹ̀yà ara (Vocabulary: family, occupations and parts of the body)
2.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. name close relatives, common occupations and the main parts of the body in Yoruba;
2. use these words in complete sentences, with jẹ́ (to be) used correctly for occupations;
3. group words by topic and explain their meanings.

## Materials

A family tree on the board, picture cards for occupations, a labelled drawing of a body, notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask pupils: Ta ni ó wà nínú ẹbí yín? (Who is in your family?) Let them name relatives in Yoruba or English. Write the words they know and use the others as the lesson's new words.

## Development

1. Revise the JSS2 vocabulary on home, school, community and environment.
2. Teach kinship words with the family tree: bàbá (father), ìyá (mother), ẹ̀gbọ́n (older brother or sister), àbúrò (younger brother or sister), arákùnrin (brother), arábìnrin (sister), bàbá ńlá (grandfather), ìyá ńlá (grandmother), ọmọ (child), ọkọ (husband), aya (wife). Explain that Yoruba distinguishes the older from the younger sibling.
3. Teach the occupations: àgbẹ̀, olùkọ́, dókítà, nọ́ọ̀sì, awakọ̀, oníṣòwò, apẹja, àránṣọ, ọlọ́pàá. Show the pattern Bàbá mi jẹ́ awakọ̀ and warn against dropping jẹ́ ("Bàbá mi awakọ̀").
4. Teach the body parts using the drawing: orí (head), ojú (eye or face), etí (ear), imú (nose), ẹnu (mouth), ọrùn (neck), apá (arm), ọwọ́ (hand), ikùn (belly), ẹ̀yìn (back), ẹsẹ̀ (leg or foot).
5. Pupils practise by pointing: "Mo fi etí gbọ́." "Mo fi ojú rí."
6. Pupils write a short paragraph about a relative and his or her work.

## Class activity

Family museum. Each pupil draws a family tree and labels each relative with a Yoruba word and one sentence about what that person does.

## Evaluation

1. What is the difference between ẹ̀gbọ́n and àbúrò?
2. Write "my mother is a teacher" in Yoruba.
3. Name three parts of the body in Yoruba.

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ẹbí wa, iṣẹ́ wa àti ara wa
reading.content:
# Ọ̀rọ̀ ẹbí, iṣẹ́ àti ẹ̀yà ara

## Ọ̀rọ̀ ìbátan

Ẹbí Yorùbá pọ̀. Èdè Yorùbá ní orúkọ fún ọ̀pọ̀ ìbátan.

| Yorùbá | English |
| --- | --- |
| bàbá | father |
| ìyá | mother |
| ẹ̀gbọ́n | older brother or sister |
| àbúrò | younger brother or sister |
| arákùnrin | brother |
| arábìnrin | sister |
| bàbá ńlá | grandfather |
| ìyá ńlá | grandmother |
| ọmọ | child |
| ọkọ | husband |
| aya | wife |

Ẹ ṣàkíyèsí pé a ní ọ̀rọ̀ méjì fún "brother or sister": ẹ̀gbọ́n fún ẹni tí ó dàgbà jù wá lọ, àbúrò fún ẹni tí ó kéré sí wa.

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ẹ̀gbọ́n mi ń kàwé ní yunifásítì. Àbúrò mi ń ṣeré ní àgbàlá.

## Iṣẹ́

| Yorùbá | English |
| --- | --- |
| àgbẹ̀ | farmer |
| olùkọ́ | teacher |
| dókítà | doctor |
| nọ́ọ̀sì | nurse |
| awakọ̀ | driver |
| oníṣòwò | trader |
| apẹja | fisherman |
| àránṣọ | tailor |
| ọlọ́pàá | police officer |

Láti sọ iṣẹ́ ẹnìkan, a máa ń lo **jẹ́**:

- Bàbá mi **jẹ́** awakọ̀. (My father is a driver.)
- Ìyá mi **jẹ́** nọ́ọ̀sì. (My mother is a nurse.)

A kò sọ pé "Bàbá mi awakọ̀". Ó yẹ kí jẹ́ wà láàrin.

## Ẹ̀yà ara

| Yorùbá | English |
| --- | --- |
| orí | head |
| ojú | eye, face |
| etí | ear |
| imú | nose |
| ẹnu | mouth |
| ọrùn | neck |
| apá | arm |
| ọwọ́ | hand |
| ikùn | belly |
| ẹ̀yìn | back |
| ẹsẹ̀ | leg, foot |

Àpẹẹrẹ: Mo fi ojú rí. Mo fi etí gbọ́. Mo fi ẹnu jẹun.

## Ìmọ̀ràn fún kíkọ́ ọ̀rọ̀

1. Fa igi ẹbí rẹ, kí o sì kọ orúkọ Yorùbá sí ẹnì kọ̀ọ̀kan.

3.topic: Lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀ àti ìránṣẹ́ (Formal letters, messages and notes)
3.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. write a short formal letter in Yoruba to a person in authority, such as the principal;
2. distinguish a formal letter from an informal one in layout and language;
3. write a clear note or message for a given situation.

## Materials

A sample formal letter and a sample informal letter side by side on the board, letter paper, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Read two openings aloud: "Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n, ṣé o wà?" and "Olórí ilé ìwé tí mo bọ̀wọ̀, mo kí yín." Ask pupils who each letter is for and how they know.

## Development

1. Revise the informal letter from JSS2: address, date, greeting, body, closing.
2. Teach the parts of a formal letter: the writer's address and date at the top right; the receiver's title and address on the left; the salutation (Olórí ilé ìwé tí mo bọ̀wọ̀); a clear subject line; the body with the request, the reason and the day; and a respectful closing (Ọmọ ilé ìwé yín tí ó ń gbọ́ràn).
3. Teach the formal language: always ẹ and yín for the person addressed; polite phrases such as Mo kí yín, Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, Mo fẹ́ tọrọ ìyọ̀ǹda (I want to ask for permission) and Ẹ ṣé.
4. Compare with the informal letter by drawing a table: who it is for, the language, the layout and the closing.
5. Practise a note: short and direct, such as telling a neighbour where a key is.
6. Pupils draft a request to the principal for permission to stay at home for a day because of illness, then swap for checking.

## Class activity

Letter doctor. The teacher gives a letter with five mistakes (no date, "o" and "rẹ" to the principal, no closing, no marks, a missing reason). Groups find and correct them.

## Evaluation

1. Where does the date go in a formal letter?
2. Which pronoun forms do you use for the principal?
3. Write a respectful closing for a letter to your principal.

## Assignment

Quiz on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀

Lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀ ni lẹ́tà tí a kọ sí ẹni tí ó ga ní ipò tàbí sí ilé iṣẹ́. Àpẹẹrẹ ni lẹ́tà sí olórí ilé ìwé, olùkọ́ àgbà, tàbí sí ọ̀gá ní ilé iṣẹ́.

## Apá lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀

1. **Adirẹ́ẹ̀sì ẹni tí ó kọ lẹ́tà** àti **déètì**: lókè ní apá ọ̀tún.
2. **Orúkọ àti adirẹ́ẹ̀sì ẹni tí a kọ lẹ́tà sí**: ní apá òsì.
3. **Ìkíni ìbẹ̀rẹ̀**: Olórí ilé ìwé tí mo bọ̀wọ̀,
4. **Àkọlé lẹ́tà (subject)**: Ìbéèrè fún ìyọ̀ǹda
5. **Ara lẹ́tà**: ìbéèrè, ìdí àti ọjọ́.
6. **Ìparí**: Ọmọ ilé ìwé yín tí ó ń gbọ́ràn, orúkọ rẹ.

## Àpẹẹrẹ

Ilé Ìwé Ìbàdàn,
Ìbàdàn.
Ọjọ́ kẹwàá oṣù Ọ̀wàrà.

Olórí ilé ìwé,
Ilé Ìwé Ìbàdàn.

Olórí ilé ìwé tí mo bọ̀wọ̀,

**Ìbéèrè fún ìyọ̀ǹda**

Mo kí yín. Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, mo fẹ́ tọrọ ìyọ̀ǹda láti wà nílé ní Ọjọ́ Ajé nítorí ara mi kò yá. Mo máa ṣe iṣẹ́ tí a bá kọ́ ní ọjọ́ náà ní ilé. Ẹ ṣé púpọ̀.

Ọmọ ilé ìwé yín tí ó ń gbọ́ràn,
Ayọ̀.

## Ìyàtọ̀ láàrin lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀ àti àìgbọ́dọ̀

| Nǹkan | Lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀ | Lẹ́tà àìgbọ́dọ̀ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ẹni tí a kọ ọ́ sí | Olórí, ọ̀gá, ilé iṣẹ́ | Ẹbí, ọ̀rẹ́ |
| Èdè | Ìbọ̀wọ̀, ẹ àti yín | Ìrọ̀rùn, o àti rẹ |
| Ìkíni | Olórí ilé ìwé tí mo bọ̀wọ̀, | Ọ̀rẹ́ mi ọ̀wọ́n, |
| Àkọlé | Ó wà | Kò sí |
| Ìparí | Ọmọ ilé ìwé yín tí ó ń gbọ́ràn, | Ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ, |

## Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú

Ìránṣẹ́ kúkúrú ń sọ ohun tí a fẹ́ sọ ní kíákíá. Ó lè jẹ́ fún ẹbí, aládùúgbò tàbí ọ̀rẹ́.

Àpẹẹrẹ: Ìyá mi, mo ti lọ sí ilé ìwé. Kọ́kọ́rọ́ wà lábẹ́ ìkòkò àdùbí. Ayọ̀.

## Àwọn àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

1. Lílo "o" àti "rẹ" fún olórí ilé ìwé.
2. Àìkọ déètì tàbí àìkọ ìdí.
3. Kíkọ lẹ́tà gígùn tí kò ní kókó.
4. Àìlo àmì ohùn.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Lẹ́tà gbọ́dọ̀ ní ìbọ̀wọ̀, ìlànà tí ó ṣe kedere àti ìdí fún ìbéèrè.

4.topic: Ewì, orin àti oríkì (Poems, songs and praise poetry)
4.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. say what ewì, orin and oríkì are and tell them apart;
2. read a short Yoruba poem aloud, state its theme and pick out repetition and other devices;
3. write a four-line poem of praise with repetition.

## Materials

The poem "Ìyá mi" written on a chart, a drum or a ruler for keeping rhythm, strips with the terms (ewì, orin, oríkì, àtúnsọ), notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Invite a pupil to sing or recite a short song or praise they know. Ask the class: is it a song, a poem or a praise? What tells you? Collect observations about rhythm, repetition and praise words.

## Development

1. Define the terms. Ewì is poetry, shaped carefully and pleasing to the ear. Orin is a song, with a tune. Oríkì is praise poetry that names the qualities of a person, family, animal or town; it is often chanted at ceremonies and on important days.
2. Read the poem "Ìyá mi" aloud with a steady beat. Pupils echo each line.
3. Ask questions: Ta ni a ń yìn? Kí ni ó ṣe fún akéwì? What words repeat? How does the poet feel? Write the answers.
4. Teach the devices: àtúnsọ (repetition), such as "Ìyá mi, ìyá mi"; àfiwé (comparison); the rhythm of short lines; praise words.
5. Discuss themes: ìfẹ́ (love), ọpẹ́ (thanks), ìbọ̀wọ̀ (respect), iṣẹ́ (work).
6. Pupils write their own four-line poem of praise for a parent, a teacher or a farmer, using repetition. Read two aloud.

## Class activity

Choral reading. Divide the class into two groups. Group one reads the first line of each pair, group two the second, and everyone joins the repeated lines. Note how repetition feels when voices join.

## Evaluation

1. What is oríkì?
2. Give an example of repetition from the poem.
3. State the theme of "Ìyá mi".

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Ewì, orin àti oríkì

## Àwọn oríṣi mẹ́ta

**Ewì** ni ọ̀rọ̀ tí a ṣe lọ́ṣọ̀ọ́, tí a sì ń sọ ní ọ̀nà tí ó dùn létí. Ó lè jẹ́ kúkúrú tàbí gígùn.

**Orin** ni ewì tí a ń kọ pẹ̀lú ohùn orin. A máa ń kọ orin ní ayẹyẹ, ní ilé ìwé àti ní ìsìn.

**Oríkì** ni ewì ìyìn. Ó ń pe àwọn ànímọ́ ènìyàn, ẹbí, ẹranko tàbí ìlú. A máa ń kọ oríkì nígbà ìgbéyàwó, ìkómọlórúkọ, ọdún àti àwọn ayẹyẹ mìíràn.

## Ewì àpẹẹrẹ

**Ìyá mi**

Ìyá mi, ìyá mi, ọ̀wọ́n ni ọ́,
Ìwọ ni o bí mi, tí o tọ́ mi,
Ìwọ ni o fún mi ní oúnjẹ,
Ìwọ ni o kọ́ mi ní ìwà.
Ọpẹ́ ni fún ọ, ìyá mi, ọ̀wọ́n ni ọ́.

## Ṣíṣàyẹ̀wò ewì náà

- **Àkòrí (theme):** ìfẹ́ àti ọpẹ́ fún ìyá.
- **Àtúnsọ (repetition):** "Ìyá mi, ìyá mi" àti "Ìwọ ni o ..." tún ń wáyé nígbà mẹ́ta.
- **Ohun tí ìyá ṣe:** ó bí akéwì, ó tọ́ ọ, ó bọ́ ọ, ó sì kọ́ ọ ní ìwà.
- **Ìmọ̀lára akéwì:** ó ní ọpẹ́, ó sì fẹ́ràn ìyá rẹ̀.
- **Ohùn ewì:** àwọn ìlà kúkúrú ń mú kí ewì náà ní ìró tí ó dùn.

## Àwọn ọ̀nà tí a fi ń ṣe ewì dùn

1. **Àtúnsọ:** títún ọ̀rọ̀ sọ, bíi "Ìyá mi, ìyá mi".
2. **Àfiwé:** fífi nǹkan kan wé òmíràn, bíi "Ó lágbára bí kìnnìún".
3. **Ìró àti ìlù:** àwọn ìlà kúkúrú tí a lè pe pẹ̀lú ìlù.
4. **Ọ̀rọ̀ ìyìn:** àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bí "ọ̀wọ́n" àti "alágbára".

## Àwọn àkòrí tí ewì Yorùbá sábà máa ń dá lé

- Ìfẹ́ àti ọpẹ́
- Ìbọ̀wọ̀ fún àgbà
- Iṣẹ́ àti ìgboyà
- Ìlú àti ìtàn

## Bí a ṣe ń kọ ewì ìyìn

1. Yan ẹni tí o fẹ́ yin: bàbá, olùkọ́, àgbẹ̀.
2. Kọ ọ̀rọ̀ ìyìn díẹ̀ nípa rẹ̀.
3. Yan ọ̀rọ̀ kan tàbí gbólóhùn kan láti tún sọ.
4. Kọ àwọn ìlà kúkúrú mẹ́rin sí márùn-ún.
5. Parí pẹ̀lú ọpẹ́ tàbí àdúrà.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Ewì ń lo àtúnsọ, àfiwé, ìró àti ìyìn. Oríkì jẹ́ ewì ìyìn.

5.topic: Eré ìtàgé Yorùbá: ìtàn inú eré, àwọn ẹ̀dá ìtàn àti àkòrí (Drama: plot, characters and theme)
5.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. read a short Yoruba play and identify its characters, scenes and stage directions;
2. retell the plot in order: the beginning, the problem and the ending;
3. describe a character from what he or she says and does, and state the theme of the play.

## Materials

The play "Òtítọ́ ni ọ̀nà" printed or on a chart (an original short play written for this lesson), role cards for three characters, notebooks, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: have you ever watched a play, a film or Nollywood scene in Yoruba? Which scene did you remember best, and why? Take two or three answers and note the words for characters, scenes and stage directions that come up.

## Development

1. Introduce the terms: eré ìtàgé (drama), ẹ̀dá ìtàn (character), ìran (scene), ìtọ́ni ìgbésẹ̀ (stage direction, the words in brackets), àkòrí (theme), ìtàn inú eré (plot).
2. Read the first scene aloud with three volunteers. Ask pupils to listen for who speaks, where the scene is set and how Ayọ̀ behaves.
3. Read the second scene and discuss: Kí ni ìṣòro náà? (What is the problem?)
4. Show the three parts of the plot on the board: ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ (start), ìṣòro (problem) and ìparí (ending).
5. Discuss the characters. Ayọ̀ first avoids telling his mother the truth but later admits what he did. How does his behaviour change?
6. Pupils write the theme in one sentence and give two reasons from the play.

## Class activity

Act the play in groups of three. After each scene the class says one thing the actors did well and one thing to improve. Then swap roles.

## Evaluation

1. Name the characters in the play.
2. What is the problem in scene two?
3. State the theme.

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Òtítọ́ ni ọ̀nà

**Àwọn ẹ̀dá ìtàn:** Ayọ̀ (akẹ́kọ̀ọ́), Ìyá Ayọ̀, Olùkọ́.

## ÌRAN KÌÍNÍ (Nílé Ayọ̀, ní ìrọ̀lẹ́)

**Ìyá:** Ayọ̀, báwo ni ìdánwò rẹ ṣe lọ?

**Ayọ̀:** (Ó yẹra fún ojú ìyá rẹ̀.) Ó lọ dáadáa, ìyá.

**Ìyá:** Ṣé o kàwé dáadáa kí o tó lọ?

**Ayọ̀:** (Ó dákẹ́ fún ìṣẹ́jú kan.) Mo kàwé díẹ̀, ìyá.

## ÌRAN KEJÌ (Ní ilé ìwé, ní ọjọ́ kejì)

**Olùkọ́:** Ayọ̀, wá síbí. Mo rí i pé ìdáhùn rẹ àti ti ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ jọra gan-an.

**Ayọ̀:** (Ó gbé orí sílẹ̀.) Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, olùkọ́, ẹ má bínú. Mo wo ìwé rẹ̀ ní ìdánwò.

**Olùkọ́:** Ó dára pé o sọ òtítọ́. Ṣùgbọ́n ìwà náà kò dára.

**Ayọ̀:** Mo ti kọ́ ẹ̀kọ́ mi. N kò ní ṣe é mọ́.

## ÌRAN KẸTA (Nílé, ní alẹ́)

**Ayọ̀:** Ìyá, mo fẹ́ sọ òtítọ́ fún yín. Mo wo ìwé ọ̀rẹ́ mi ní ìdánwò.

**Ìyá:** Mo dúpẹ́ pé o sọ òtítọ́ fún mi. Ọmọ rere ni ọ́. Òtítọ́ ni ọ̀nà.

## Àyẹ̀wò eré náà

**Ìtàn inú eré (plot):**

1. **Ìbẹ̀rẹ̀:** ìyá bi Ayọ̀ nípa ìdánwò rẹ̀, Ayọ̀ sì yẹra fún òtítọ́.
2. **Ìṣòro:** olùkọ́ rí i pé ìdáhùn Ayọ̀ jọ ti ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀, Ayọ̀ sì jẹ́wọ́ pé ó wo ìwé rẹ̀.
3. **Ìparí:** Ayọ̀ sọ òtítọ́ fún ìyá rẹ̀, ìyá sì dúpẹ́ lọ́wọ́ rẹ̀.

**Àwọn ẹ̀dá ìtàn:**

- **Ayọ̀:** ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ó yẹra fún òtítọ́ (ó yẹra fún ojú ìyá rẹ̀). Lẹ́yìn náà ó jẹ́wọ́, ó sì kábàámọ̀ (ó gbé orí sílẹ̀).
- **Ìyá Ayọ̀:** ó fẹ́ràn ọmọ rẹ̀, ó sì fẹ́ kí ó jẹ́ olóòtítọ́.
- **Olùkọ́:** ó ń fi ìbínú díẹ̀ hàn, ṣùgbọ́n ó dúpẹ́ pé Ayọ̀ sọ òtítọ́.

6.topic: Pàtàkì lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn Yorùbá (The cultural significance of oral literature)
6.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. name the main kinds of Yoruba oral literature: òwe, àlọ́, ewì, ìjálá, rárà and oríkì;
2. explain the functions of oral literature: teaching, preserving history, entertaining and uniting people;
3. give examples of how oral literature is used in Yoruba life today.

## Materials

Cards with the names of the genres, pictures of a hunter, an elder telling a story and a naming ceremony, a recording of a chant if possible, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: where did you last hear a proverb, a riddle or a chant? At home, in church, at a wedding, on the radio? Write the places on the board. Show that oral literature is still around us.

## Development

1. Define lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn (oral literature): literature that is spoken, chanted or sung and passed from person to person, not written.
2. Review the genres: òwe (proverb), àlọ́ (folktale and riddle), ewì (poetry), ìjálá (hunters' chant), rárà (chant of praise) and oríkì (praise poetry).
3. Teach the functions with examples: teaching (proverbs teach good conduct), preserving history (oríkì names ancestors and towns), entertaining (àlọ́ in the evening), bringing people together (songs and chants at festivals), and sharpening the mind (riddles).
4. Discuss the dangers: young people no longer learn the genres and many elders are passing away. Suggest ways to keep them alive: recording, school clubs, festivals, naming ceremonies.
5. Pupils each state one genre they know and one function it serves.
6. Pupils write a short paragraph to explain why oral literature matters.

## Class activity

Talk to an elder. Each pupil interviews an elder at home (or a classmate who has one) and writes down one proverb, one riddle and what it means. Share in class next lesson.

## Evaluation

1. What is lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn?
2. Give two functions of oral literature.
3. How can we keep oral literature alive?

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Pàtàkì lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn Yorùbá

## Kí ni lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn?

Lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn ni àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tí a ń sọ, kọ tàbí kọrin, tí a sì ń gbé láti ẹnu ẹnìkan sí ẹlòmíràn láìkọ wọ́n sílẹ̀. Àwọn Yorùbá ní òwe, àlọ́, ewì, ìjálá, rárà, oríkì àti orin.

## Iṣẹ́ tí wọ́n ń ṣe

### 1. Wọ́n ń kọ́ni ní ìwà rere

Òwe ń kọ́ ọmọdé ní ìwà. "Iṣẹ́ ni oògùn ìṣẹ́" ń kọ́ni pé a gbọdọ̀ ṣiṣẹ́. Àwọn ìtàn àlọ́ bíi ti Ìjàpá ń kọ́ni pé olè jíjà kò dára.

### 2. Wọ́n ń pa ìtàn mọ́

Oríkì ń pe orúkọ àwọn baba ńlá wa, ẹbí wa àti ìlú wa. Nípasẹ̀ rẹ̀, ọmọ lè mọ ibi tí ó ti wá. Ìjálá ń sọ ìtàn ìgboyà àwọn ọdẹ àti iṣẹ́ wọn.

### 3. Wọ́n ń mú inú ẹni dùn

A máa ń sọ àlọ́ ní alẹ́ nígbà tí ẹbí bá péjọ. A máa ń kọrin àti ewì ní ayẹyẹ. Wọ́n ń mú kí àwọn ènìyàn rẹ́rìn-ín.

### 4. Wọ́n ń mú ìṣọ̀kan wá

Nígbà ọdún, ìgbéyàwó tàbí ìkómọlórúkọ, gbogbo ènìyàn máa ń péjọ láti gbọ́ ewì, orin àti oríkì. Èyí ń mú kí wọ́n ní ìmọ̀lára pé wọ́n jẹ́ ẹ̀yà kan náà.

### 5. Wọ́n ń mú ọgbọ́n pọ̀ sí i

Àlọ́ àpamọ̀ ń mú kí ọmọdé ronú. Ó ń kọ́ ọ láti wá ìdáhùn.

## Ìṣòro tó ń kojú wọ́n

- Àwọn ọmọdé kì í fi bẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́ wọn mọ́.
- Àwọn àgbà tí ó mọ̀ wọ́n ń kú lọ.
- Àwọn ènìyàn fẹ́ràn fídíò àti orin àjèjì ju àṣà wọn lọ.

## Bí a ṣe lè pa wọ́n mọ́

1. Ká máa sọ wọ́n nílé fún àwọn ọmọdé.
2. Ká kọ wọ́n sílẹ̀, ká sì gba wọ́n sílẹ̀ lórí ẹ̀rọ.
3. Ká ní ẹgbẹ́ ewì àti àsọyé ní ilé ìwé.
4. Ká máa lò wọ́n ní ayẹyẹ ìbílẹ̀.

## Àpẹẹrẹ

Nígbà ìkómọlórúkọ, àgbà kan lè sọ pé "Ọmọ tí a kò kọ́ ni yóò gbé ilé tà." Gbólóhùn yìí ń kọ́ àwọn òbí pé wọ́n gbọdọ̀ tọ́ ọmọ wọn dáadáa.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn ń kọ́ni, ń pa ìtàn mọ́, ń mú inú dùn, ó sì ń mú ìṣọ̀kan wá.

8.topic: Èdè Yorùbá, ìdánimọ̀ àti ogún àṣà (Language, identity and cultural heritage)
8.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. explain how the Yoruba language carries the identity and heritage of its people;
2. explain the meaning and value of Yoruba names, greetings and oral traditions;
3. discuss threats to the language and suggest ways of preserving it.

## Materials

A list of ten common Yoruba names with meanings, a chart showing a mixed Yoruba and English sentence, a recording or a short talk by an elder if available, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask pupils to say their full names and tell the class what one name means. Write three on the board with their meanings (for example Ayọ̀: joy). Ask: what does a name tell us about the language and the family?

## Development

1. Define ìdánimọ̀ (identity): what makes a person or a people recognisable: language, names, dress, food, greetings, festivals, beliefs.
2. Names. Yoruba names carry meaning and hope: Ayọ̀ (joy), Tọ́pẹ́ (worthy of thanks), Ọlá (honour), Adé (crown), Ìbùkún (blessing). Names are given at the ìkómọlórúkọ (naming ceremony) on the eighth day after birth, with prayers and symbolic foods, and the family may also pronounce oríkì for the child.
3. Greetings. The way a Yoruba child greets elders by kneeling or prostrating, and the many greetings for every occasion, show respect and community.
4. Oral literature. Proverbs, folktales, ewì and oríkì store the wisdom and history of the people.
5. Threats: many families speak mostly English at home; some children cannot read or write Yoruba; mixed speech ("Yoruba-English") grows; fewer people learn proverbs and chants.
6. Preservation: speak Yoruba daily at home, give Yoruba names with meaning, read and write Yoruba, support school clubs and festivals, record elders, and use Yoruba in media and technology.

## Class activity

Class survey. Each pupil asks three people at home how they greet in the morning and what language they speak most. Share and discuss in the next lesson.

## Evaluation

1. What is the meaning of the name Ayọ̀?
2. Name two things that make up Yoruba identity.
3. Give two ways of keeping the language alive.

## Assignment

Worksheet on the app, due Friday.

reading.content:
# Èdè Yorùbá, ìdánimọ̀ àti ogún àṣà

## Kí ni ìdánimọ̀?

**Ìdánimọ̀** ni ohun tí ó mú kí a mọ ènìyàn tàbí ẹ̀yà kan. Èdè, orúkọ, aṣọ, oúnjẹ, ìkíni, ọdún àti ìgbàgbọ́ jẹ́ ara ìdánimọ̀ Yorùbá.

Èdè ni ọ̀kan nínú àwọn pàtàkì jù. Nípasẹ̀ rẹ̀ ni àwọn òbí fi ń kọ́ ọmọ ní ìwà, ìtàn àti ọgbọ́n ìbílẹ̀. Bí èdè kan bá parẹ́, apá ńlá nínú àṣà rẹ̀ lè parẹ́ pẹ̀lú.

## Orúkọ Yorùbá

Orúkọ Yorùbá ní ìtumọ̀, ó sì ń fi ìrètí àwọn òbí hàn.

| Orúkọ | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| Ayọ̀ | joy |
| Tọ́pẹ́ | worthy of thanks |
| Ọlá | honour, wealth |
| Adé | crown |
| Ìbùkún | blessing |

A máa ń fún ọmọ lórúkọ ní **ìkómọlórúkọ**, ní ọjọ́ kẹjọ lẹ́yìn ìbí. Wọ́n máa ń gbàdúrà fún ọmọ náà, wọ́n sì máa ń lo oúnjẹ tí ó ní ìtumọ̀ àmì. Ẹbí lè pe oríkì ọmọ náà.

## Ìkíni àti ìbọ̀wọ̀

Ọmọ Yorùbá ń dọ̀bálẹ̀ tàbí kúnlẹ̀ láti kí àgbà. Ìkíni wà fún gbogbo ìgbà, bíi **Ẹ káàárọ̀**, **Ẹ kú iṣẹ́** àti **Ẹ kú àbọ̀**. Àwọn ìkíni wọ̀nyí ń fi ọ̀wọ̀ àti ìfẹ́ hàn.

## Lítíréṣọ̀ alohùn

Òwe, àlọ́, ewì, ìjálá, rárà àti oríkì ń pa ọgbọ́n àti ìtàn àwọn baba wa mọ́.

## Àwọn ewu fún èdè Yorùbá

1. Ọ̀pọ̀ ẹbí ń sọ Gẹ̀ẹ́sì jù nílé.
2. Àwọn ọmọ kan kò lè kàwé tàbí kọ̀wé ní Yorùbá.
3. Àwọn ènìyàn ń pò Yorùbá àti Gẹ̀ẹ́sì mọ́ ara wọn nígbà tí wọ́n bá ń sọ̀rọ̀.
4. Àwọn ọ̀dọ́ kì í fi bẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́ òwe àti oríkì mọ́.

## Bí a ṣe lè pa èdè mọ́

1. Ká máa sọ Yorùbá lójoojúmọ́ nílé.
2. Ká fún ọmọ ní orúkọ Yorùbá tí ó ní ìtumọ̀.
3. Ká kọ́ ọmọ láti kàwé àti kọ̀wé ní Yorùbá, pẹ̀lú àmì ohùn tí ó tọ́.
4. Ká ṣètìlẹ́yìn fún ẹgbẹ́ èdè ní ilé ìwé àti ọdún ìbílẹ̀.
5. Ká gba ohùn àwọn àgbà sílẹ̀ kí a sì kọ ìtàn wọn sílẹ̀.
6. Ká lo Yorùbá lórí ẹ̀rọ alátagbà àti lórí ayélujára.

## Àpẹẹrẹ

Nígbà tí ọmọ kan bá sọ pé "Mo wà ní kíláàsì kínní" dípò "I'm in class one", ó ń fi èdè rẹ̀ lò. Bí gbogbo ọmọ bá ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, èdè Yorùbá yóò wà láàyè.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Èdè jẹ́ ara ìdánimọ̀ wa. Bí a bá ń lò ó, kọ ọ́, tí a sì kọ́ ọmọ wa ní i, yóò wà títí.

9.topic: Ìkíni fún onírúurú ayẹyẹ àti àyè (Greetings for different occasions)
9.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. choose the right greeting and reply for a festival, a wedding, an illness, a bereavement and a farewell;
2. use ẹ and yín correctly when greeting elders;
3. write and act a short dialogue that includes a greeting for a special occasion.

## Materials

Occasion cards (Ọdún, Ìgbéyàwó, Àìsàn, Ìbànújẹ́, Ìdágbére), a small mat for kneeling or prostrating (optional), role cards, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Ask: what would you say to a neighbour who has just got married? To one who is ill? To one who is leaving for a journey? Write the answers (in English or Yoruba) and show that each occasion has its own words.

## Development

1. Revise the JSS1 greetings (Ẹ káàárọ̀, Ẹ kú ọ̀sán, Ẹ kú ìrọ̀lẹ́, Ẹ kú iṣẹ́, Ẹ kú àbọ̀) and the idea that the greeting changes with time and occasion.
2. Teach the occasion greetings and replies: Ìgbéyàwó: Ẹ kú oríire. Ọdún: Ẹ kú ọdún, with the reply Ọdún á yabọ̀. Àìsàn: Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́, ara á yá. Ìbànújẹ́ (loss): Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́, Ọlọ́run á tù yín nínú. Ìdágbére: Ó dàbọ̀.
3. Revise ẹ and yín for elders and o and rẹ for friends of the same age.
4. Demonstrate with two volunteers: a child greeting a grandparent on a festival day, asking after the family and saying goodbye.
5. Discuss tone and manner: a gentle voice for bereavement, a joyful voice for a wedding; do not laugh when sympathising.
6. Pupils write a six-line dialogue for an occasion of their choice.

reading.content:
# Ìkíni fún onírúurú ayẹyẹ

Ọmọlúwàbí mọ ìkíni tó yẹ fún gbogbo àkókò. Ìkíni tí a bá lò fún ìgbéyàwó kò lè jẹ́ èyí tí a ó lò fún ìsìnkú. Ẹ jẹ́ kí a mọ àwọn tó wọ́pọ̀.

## Ìkíni fún ayẹyẹ

| Àkókò | Ìkíni | Ìdáhùn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ìgbéyàwó, ìbí ọmọ, ìgbéga | Ẹ kú oríire | Ẹ ṣé |
| Ọdún | Ẹ kú ọdún | Ọdún á yabọ̀ |
| Ìparí iṣẹ́ | Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ | Ẹ ṣé |
| Ẹni tí ó dé láti ìrìn-àjò | Ẹ kú àbọ̀ | Ẹ ṣé |

## Ìkíni nígbà ìṣòro

| Àkókò | Ìkíni | Ìdáhùn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Àìsàn | Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́, ara á yá | Àṣẹ, ẹ ṣé |
| Ìbànújẹ́ (ikú ẹbí) | Ẹ pẹ̀lẹ́, Ọlọ́run á tù yín nínú | Àṣẹ, ẹ ṣé |

**Àṣẹ** túmọ̀ sí "Amen" tàbí "Let it be so".

## Ìdágbére (parting)

- **Ó dàbọ̀** (Goodbye). A máa ń dáhùn pé: **Ó dàbọ̀**.
- Fún ẹni tí ó ń lọ sí ìrìn-àjò: **Ẹ kú ọ̀nà.**

## Bí a ṣe ń kí àgbà

1. Ọmọkùnrin lè dọ̀bálẹ̀, ọmọbìnrin sì lè kúnlẹ̀.
2. A máa ń lo **ẹ** àti **yín** fún àgbà.
3. A máa ń bèèrè nípa ìlera ẹbí: **Báwo ni ẹbí?**
4. A kì í dá ọ̀rọ̀ àgbà dúró.

## Ìmọ̀ràn nípa ìwà

- Fún ayẹyẹ ayọ̀ bíi ìgbéyàwó, ohùn wa lè jẹ́ ti ayọ̀.
- Fún ìbànújẹ́ àti àìsàn, ohùn wa gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ ti ìbànújẹ́ àti ìtùnú.
- A kì í rẹ́rìn-ín nígbà tí a bá ń kí ẹni tí ó ní ìbànújẹ́.

## Ìjíròrò àpẹẹrẹ

Ọmọ: Ẹ kú ọdún, bàbá ńlá.
Bàbá ńlá: Ọdún á yabọ̀, ọmọ mi. Báwo ni ilé ìwé?
Ọmọ: Ó dára, bàbá ńlá. Mo ń kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ dáadáa.
Bàbá ńlá: Ó dára. Ọlọ́run á bùkún ọ.
Ọmọ: Àṣẹ. Ó dàbọ̀, bàbá ńlá.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Àkókò tí a wà ni ó ń pinnu ìkíni tí a ó lò. Fún àgbà, a máa ń lo ẹ àti yín.

10.topic: Ìdánrawò ohùn àti ìró èdè Yorùbá (Oral drills: sounds, syllables and tone contrasts)
10.lessonNote:
## Objectives

By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:

1. divide Yoruba words into syllables and count them;
2. contrast words that differ only by tone (kọ, kọ́, kọ̀), by an oral or nasal vowel (ìrì, ìrìn) or by s and ṣ (sè, ṣe);
3. pronounce words with even rhythm and the correct tones, and write them correctly.

## Materials

Syllable cards (cut into pieces), a drum or a ruler for tapping syllables, a chart of minimal pairs, slates, chalk.

## Starter (5 minutes)

Tap out the rhythm of the word ọmọ and ask pupils how many taps. Do the same for ilé, ọkùnrin and akẹ́kọ̀ọ́. Write the numbers on the board, then explain that each tap is a syllable.

## Development

1. Revise the three tones, the oral and nasal vowels, and the under-dotted letters from JSS1 and JSS2.
2. Teach the syllable. A Yoruba syllable is a vowel alone (V), a consonant and a vowel (CV) or a syllabic nasal (N). Divide: ọ-mọ (2), i-lé (2), ọ-kùn-rin (3), o-lù-kọ́ (3), a-kẹ́-kọ̀-ọ́ (4).
3. Drill the tone triple: kọ (to write), kọ́ (to build or to teach), kọ̀ (to refuse). Use hand movements: level, rising, falling.
4. Drill the nasal contrast: ìrì (dew) and ìrìn (walking, journey). Pupils feel the nose vibrate on the final n.
5. Drill sè (to cook) and ṣe (to do, to make). Pupils hold a hand in front of the mouth to feel the difference between s and ṣ.
6. Speak with even rhythm: each syllable has about the same length and a steady tone, with no English stress. Have pupils clap syllables as they say a sentence.

## Class activity

Syllable relay. Each team builds a word from syllable cards and says it aloud, tapping each syllable. A second team writes it with its marks. The first team to do both correctly scores.

## Evaluation

1. How many syllables are in olùkọ́?
2. What are the meanings of kọ, kọ́ and kọ̀?
3. Say the difference between sè and ṣe.

## Assignment

Problem set on the app, due Friday.

reading.title: Ohùn, sílébù àti ìró
reading.content:
# Ohùn, sílébù àti ìró

## Sílébù

Sílébù ni ìpín ọ̀rọ̀ tí a lè pè ní ẹ̀ẹ̀kan. Ní èdè Yorùbá, sílébù lè jẹ́:

- fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì nìkan (V), bíi **a**, **ọ**;
- kọ́ńsónáǹtì àti fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì (CV), bíi **lé**, **mọ**;
- kọ́ńsónáǹtì aránmúpè (N), bíi **ń** nínú *Mo ń lọ*.

### Pípín ọ̀rọ̀ sí sílébù

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Sílébù | Iye |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ọmọ | ọ-mọ | 2 |
| ilé | i-lé | 2 |
| ọkùnrin | ọ-kùn-rin | 3 |
| olùkọ́ | o-lù-kọ́ | 3 |
| akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ | a-kẹ́-kọ̀-ọ́ | 4 |

## Ohùn tó yàtọ̀ sí ara wọn

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| kọ | to write |
| kọ́ | to build, to teach |
| kọ̀ | to refuse |

Àpẹẹrẹ:

- Mo **kọ** ìwé. (I wrote a letter.)
- Olùkọ́ **kọ́** wa ní Yorùbá. (The teacher taught us Yoruba.)
- Ó **kọ̀** láti jẹun. (He refused to eat.)

## Fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àìránmúpè àti àránmúpè

| Àìránmúpè | Àránmúpè |
| --- | --- |
| ìrì (dew) | ìrìn (walking, journey) |

Nígbà tí a bá ń pe **ìrìn**, afẹ́fẹ́ gba ímú kọjá. Nígbà tí a bá ń pe **ìrì**, afẹ́fẹ́ gba ẹnu nìkan.

## s àti ṣ

| Ọ̀rọ̀ | Ìtumọ̀ |
| --- | --- |
| sè | to cook |
| ṣe | to do, to make |

Ìyá mi ń **sè** oúnjẹ. Bàbá mi ń **ṣe** iṣẹ́.

## Bí a ṣe ń pe ọ̀rọ̀ Yorùbá

1. Sílébù kọ̀ọ̀kan gbọdọ̀ gùn bákan náà.
2. A kì í fi ohùn gíga pe sílébù kan bíi ti Gẹ̀ẹ́sì.
3. Pe sílébù kọ̀ọ̀kan pẹ̀lú ohùn rẹ̀ tó tọ́.
4. Ka sílébù pẹ̀lú ìpàtẹ́wọ́ láti mọ iye wọn.

## Àwọn àṣìṣe tí ó wọ́pọ̀

- Kíka sílébù ní àṣìṣe: *ọkùnrin* ní sílébù mẹ́ta, kì í ṣe méjì.
- Pípe *ṣe* bí *se*.
- Pípe *ìrìn* bí *ìrì*, tí a kò fi ohùn ímú sí i.
- Fífi àfikún sílébù kún ọ̀rọ̀.

## Ohun tí a gbọdọ̀ rántí

Sílébù jẹ́ V, CV tàbí N. Ohùn, fáwẹ́ẹ̀lì àránmúpè àti s/ṣ ń yí ìtumọ̀ ọ̀rọ̀ padà.
